brief: A kitchen herb planter: two or three bins on a base, filled with soil and planted with basil and thyme.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.requirement: Two or three bins on a base
requirements.evidence: 3 full-depth bins: bin:0,0,0, bin:0,1,0, bin:1,0,0 on pieces at same cells
fillSoil applied to all three bins
basil-harvest in bin:0,0,0, thyme-harvest in bin:0,1,0, basil-young in bin:1,0,0 – both herbs present

finish.summary: Three-cell L-shaped base with three full-depth bins, each filled with soil and planted: basil and thyme as requested, with an extra basil plant in the third bin.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Your herb planter is on the way — I'll set up a soil-filled base for your basil and thyme.
